postTitle: Geographic Arbitrage: Living Abroad to Save More
topic: Earning in one currency and spending in another: the same local prices can cost more

assumptions.notes: Reel's own example, illustrative: €2,000 of monthly bills in local money; the local currency rises 25%, so the same bills cost €2,500. The lesson's figure: major currencies can move 20 to 30% over a few years.

hookVariants.narration: Your monthly bills abroad cost two thousand euros. Could unchanged local prices still cost you more?
onscreenLines: Can the same local prices cost you more?

beats.narration: The bills stay the same in local money.
But buying that local money now costs five hundred euros more.

callout.label: more for the same local money

beats.narration: So those same bills now take two thousand five hundred euros.

callout.label: more for the same local money

beats.narration: With unchanged euro pay, five hundred less is left to save.

cta.narration: Send this to someone who earns and spends in different currencies.

caption.instagram:
Your monthly bills abroad cost €2,000. Can the same local prices cost you more?

The example: the bills do not change in local money, but the local currency rises against the euro, so buying it costs €500 more. The same bills now take €2,500, and with unchanged euro pay, €500 less is left each month.

Major currencies can move 20 to 30% over a few years without any crisis, in either direction. Two habits people describe: converting savings as needed, not all at once, and in retirement holding more of the currency they spend in.
